source_role: AIGMos Build Tool integration requirements; NOT a CW Ruleset edit

owns: AIGMos Build Tool consumption of source markup

source_refs: CW_CodeMarkup_Prune_Requirements_Handover_v0.1.0.json (2026-11-23 handoff delivered separately to CW development)

confirmed_by_user.rule: Single Python # comment prefix for metadata and markup, never a special ## prefix.
First three metadata lines retain exact order: # deps, # libs, # target; optional # prune JSON string array follows.
The Git checkout is CPython-first. In a file supporting both targets, CP body is executable Python and MP body is commented source activated by MP build.
Use # target: BOTH for files with shared MP/CP implementations and # <AC.CP>/# </AC.CP> and # <AC.MP>/# </AC.MP> for platform variations. AC is an example feature ID.
A root feature entry in # prune such as AC controls its AC.CP and AC.MP code variants; the target suffix is a variant selector, not a separately chosen feature.
Build Tool physically removes excluded branches, optional hooks and exclusive dependencies; raw code is not rewritten by executing it.
CodeMarkup already belongs on the CW roadmap; AIGMos only sends its new real use-case requirements to CW. Do not modify CW specs in this repo/session.

example.source:
# deps: ["HC.STATE"]
# libs: []
# target: BOTH
# prune: ["AC"]

def execute(command):

    # <AC.CP>
    authorize_cp(command)
    # </AC.CP>

    # <AC.MP>
    # authorize_mp(command)
    # </AC.MP>

    return dispatch(command)
example.raw_checkout: CPython interprets the CP statement, and the MP statement is a comment.
example.build_cp_ac: CP branch stays; MP branch and markup removed.
example.build_mp_ac: CP branch removed; MP comment is activated by removing its single agreed comment prefix.

target_migration.historical_contract: Source_Dependency_Header_v0.2.0: MP=compatible with MP and CP; CP=CP-only. BOTH does not exist there.
target_migration.proposed_next_version: Explicitly version a three-value target scheme MP=MP-only, CP=CP-only, BOTH=supported on MP and CP (with target-specific blocks as needed).
target_migration.compatibility_gate: NEVER reinterpret header v0.2.0 target=MP retroactively. Scanner must use pinned header/markup contract versions.
target_migration.raw_checkout_scope: CP-first is a rule for the normal full-system source/entrypoint; it does not imply MP-only files are independently executable under CPython.

order: Scan headers and CodeMarkup with pinned ruleset
Resolve canonical feature IDs against StructureTree projection
Compute direct typed dependencies and derived dependency closure
Select feature and target branches and physically emit code
Re-scan emitted code and validate imports/commands/resources
Parse/compile generated Python and enforce target/runtime checks
source_processing.dependency_authority: Code-file header declares direct code dependencies. StructureTree is derived and cannot silently override actual source claims. Closure is computed, never treated as independent SSOT.
source_processing.conditional_dependency_gap: Exact declaration of branch-specific direct deps/libs is unresolved. # prune itself is NOT a full substitute for deps/libs.
source_processing.scope_boundary: In-file pruning in Hardcore and whole module/file pruning starting at Core Modules is an AIGMos initial use-case policy proposal, not a global CW rule or a validated hard prohibition.

validator_requirements: Unknown feature IDs and malformed JSON => FAIL
Tag feature missing from # prune => FAIL absent explicitly versioned exception
Generated code has valid syntax and no leaked unwanted feature/import/command reference
Direct dependencies, platform capabilities, module authorization and closure validated separately
Raw default CP file must parse; all required emitted target variants must parse
No implicit automatic fix of invalid suites or magical import installation
Original source span -> emitted line/region provenance recorded
Historical header semantic versions must remain distinguishable
open_for_CW_or_AIGMos: CW formal CodeMarkup syntax: nesting, escaping comments, multiline syntax, indentation, raw Python token contexts
How conditional direct deps/libs are explicitly represented and checked
Exact versioned migration from header v0.2.0 to new target vocabulary
Line source mapping/format and emitted metadata policy
Detailed allowed markup scope at Core Module boundary
Compiler/device acceptance implementation and negative tests
lifecycle: Development draft; no executable validator, CW ruleset change or LOCKED status implied.
